song_story.overview: Yours is a slow-building R&B surrender song — the narrator gives up any pretense of control over the relationship and hands themselves over completely, repeating 'I'll be yours' like a vow. The multiple featured voices (a producer, an idol vocalist, a solo singer, a rapper) trade sections instead of one artist carrying the whole thing, which gives the devotion a layered, almost call-and-response quality, like several different people arriving at the same conclusion from different angles.
song_story.cultural_root: The song leans on 헌신 (heonsin) — total devotion or self-sacrifice for someone else — pushed to a deliberately hyperbolic extreme. The line '내 탄생은 널 위해 이루어진 게 아닐까' (wasn't my birth itself made to happen for you) is a very Korean R&B move: love isn't described as a choice or a compatible match, it's framed as destiny reaching backward to claim even your birth. That scale of overstatement is a genre convention, meant to be felt as intensity rather than taken literally.

verse_1.literal: Hidden behind lips / a whisper in the eyes / I'll be yours / I'll be yours
verse_1.context: The opening pairs a physical image (lips hiding something) with an emotional one (eyes whispering) before the English hook even arrives — the declaration 'I'll be yours' gets set up as something communicated silently, through expression, before it's ever said in words.

verse_2.literal: Is there anything more painful / than indifferent attention / time like black and white / not knowing even an inch ahead
verse_2.context: 무심한 관심 (indifferent attention) is a small contradiction on purpose — being noticed by someone who doesn't actually care is framed as its own specific kind of pain, worse than being ignored outright. 흑백 같은 시간 (time like black and white) suggests a period drained of color, waiting without any sense of what's coming.

chorus.literal: As if everything is caught in darkness / with both eyes closed / drunk on feelings with the lights turned off / I'm losing you
chorus.context: 불 꺼진 감정 (feelings with the light turned off) extends the darkness imagery into something almost intoxicating — 취하다 (to get drunk/intoxicated) applied to an emotional state rather than alcohol. Losing someone here isn't sudden, it happens with your eyes deliberately closed, half-willingly.

bridge.literal: This feeling hidden tightly inside / on that day, without fail / tell me to bring it out / how should I even start to say it
bridge.context: 숨긴 마음 (a feeling hidden away) sits at the center of the R&B genre's tension between wanting total devotion and being unable to actually voice it. The rhetorical question at the end — not knowing how to even begin the conversation — undercuts the confident 'I'll be yours' hook with real hesitation.

hyperbole_line.literal: Wasn't my birth itself / made to happen for you / that kind of talking to myself
hyperbole_line.context: This is the song's most extreme claim — framing your own existence as having been arranged for one specific person — immediately labeled 혼잣말 (talking to oneself, muttering), which softens the grandiosity by admitting it's a private, almost embarrassing thought rather than something said out loud to the person.

artist_context: Raiden is a Korean-American producer who has shaped sounds for major K-pop acts from behind the scenes, occasionally stepping forward with collaborative singles under his own name. Yours brings together EXO's Chanyeol, solo vocalist LEE HI, and rapper Changmo on one track, a format that mirrors Western producer-led compilation singles more than a typical group comeback.
honorific_level: informal — 반말 throughout, intimate and unguarded

grammar_highlights.usage: 'While remaining in a state of...' 한 치 앞도 모른 채 (not knowing even an inch ahead, while) describes an ongoing condition someone is stuck in, not a single completed action.
Marks a gradual, ongoing process. 잃어가 ('losing, bit by bit') frames losing someone as a slow slide rather than a single moment.

'Isn't it that...?' — a rhetorical, hedged way to voice a strong private belief. 이루어진 게 아닐까 floats an extreme claim (fate arranged my birth for you) as a question rather than a flat assertion, softening its intensity.
